_help: The client-portal workflow as data. docs/ROADMAP.md is the same thing written for people; this file is what tools/check-client.js evaluates and what an automation reads. Paths use {slug}. Every gate check has a type that check-client.js implements; 'manual' checks are listed for a person to tick and never pass on their own. Change the workflow here and in the roadmap together, and bump version.

markers.TODO: A value starting TODO is ours to write. It must be gone before anyone outside the team sees the portal (Phase 3 gate).
markers.demo: demo:true is ours-written, theirs-to-confirm placeholder content. It may ship to a showcase; it must be gone or explicitly accepted at sign-off (Phase 8 gate).
markers._help: A _help key is a template instruction. It is deleted when its section is completed (Phase 1 gate for the brand file).
markers.PLACEHOLDER: A stand-in value or asset written by tools/new-client.js. Replaced in Phase 1.

phases.title: Intake and kickoff
phases.goal: Agree what is being built, for whom, by when, and start every request to the client on day one so nothing waits on them later.
phases.owner: us, with the client's main contact
inputs: Name of the main contact and of whoever signs off

steps.title: Choose the slug: short, lowercase, permanent. It is in every file name and the subdomain.
Scaffold the client
Send the asks list the same day: master logos, guideline, photos, SOPs, system names, a sample export, domain and DNS owner
Run the kickoff and fill {slug}-intake.md: audiences, what they call their customers, features on or off, dates
Copy the open asks into brand meta.confirmWithClient so the sheet and the handover pack print them

gate.label: every intake question answered, or marked n/a with a reason

gate.text: Asks list sent to the client, with a date to chase

onyx.note: Not a separate step for ONYX: the capture started from the public site and the asks went into meta.confirmWithClient. Written down here so the next client gets it on day one.

phases.title: Brand portfolio
phases.goal: One source of truth for how the client looks, sounds and behaves, signed off by the client, that the portal and every simulation read from.
inputs: Sixteen or more phone captures of the client's site
Master logo files and guideline when they arrive

steps.title: Collect sources and save cropped captures and a contact sheet to assets/reference/
Sample colours with a pixel histogram, not an eyedropper; record hex and RGB
Identify the typeface and the weights in use; add its woff2 files to template/portal/fonts/
Fill {slug}-brand.json, deleting each _help as its section is done; derive the portal tones including primaryTint, primaryDeep and ctaDeep
Build tokens and read the contrast report; every failing site pattern gets a portal variant
Redraw the logo and mark stand-ins as SVG over a 10% grid
Build the brand sheet from ONYX's, keeping the @tokens markers, and render it at 390px and 1280px
Write {slug}-brand.md from the sheet, with provenance and the open items
Enter the six SimStudio decisions, save the kit under the client's name, export it beside the brand file
Render the app icons from the mark
Send the sheet for sign-off; corrections go into the JSON, the build runs, the version bumps, the changelog gets a line

gate.label: tint and deep roles have their own colours
reference captures and a contact sheet
SimStudio kit exported beside the brand file

gate.text: Sheet rendered and checked at 390px and 1280px
Sheet sent to the client for sign-off

onyx.effort: one working day from the public site
onyx.note: Sixteen mobile captures; Poppins; green, amber and black pixel-sampled; white on green and white on amber failed AA and became ink in the portal.

phases.title: Portal structure
phases.goal: The portal's skeleton decided and built: who comes in, through which doors, behind which keys, and what each of them sees on Home and in the tab bar.
inputs: Intake: audiences, their names for things, features on or off

steps.title: Fill the client block: names, site, address, website, member login, tagline, demoNote
Set the audiences: member (no key, first), employee, manager, owner; keys, sees, doorGroup, learnModules
Set nav per audience, five tabs at most; choose homeTiles, homeCards or the path list per audience
Set areas (usually four) and groups named after the job
Turn optional modules on or off: reports, processes, news, floorplans
Build

gate.label: single-file build matches the current config

gate.text: Audiences, keys and module choices agreed with the client

onyx.note: Started with three audiences; members arrived on day three, sees replaced the implied rule, doorGroup came last.

phases.title: Content authoring
phases.goal: Every item, path, support answer, process and post written in the client's voice, with nothing of ours left to write.
inputs: The client's SOPs, onboarding notes, checklists and FAQs

steps.title: Write the first path: ten to eighteen items in the order a new starter meets them
Write guides, checklists and articles to the content standards; mark everything unconfirmed demo
Write the manager and owner content
Write member tips and their own Support page
Write Support: the questions first, then problem-led Direct assistance, with placeholder contacts on reserved ranges
Write the process library: every process drives named items; include real drafts and gaps
Write the first posts
Build

gate.label: no TODO left anywhere in the config
every process drives items that exist

gate.text: Read through once in the client's voice against the brand voice rules

onyx.note: 57 items, 3 paths, 29 processes (22 documented, 4 drafts, 3 gaps), 5 posts. A wrong fact (RECOVER is booked, not walk-in) was in five places and fixed in all of them.

phases.title: Simulations and media
phases.goal: Every simulation, interactive photo and video in place of its placeholder, wearing the client's kit, and working inside the portal's frame at phone width.
phases.owner: us in SimStudio; the client supplies access and photos
inputs: Access to the client's systems or recordings of them

steps.title: Record each simulation in SimStudio with the client's kit; bars hidden while embedded
Export to content/sims/{slug}-sim-<item-id>.html and keep the .simproj.json in content/sims/src/
Photographs as JPEG, never PNG; check the export's size against the budget
Point each item at its file, set demo false, rebuild
Check each export in the frame at phone width; record any hand fix in content/README.md

gate.label: no simulation still on the placeholder
every local src points at a file

gate.text: Every export opened in the portal frame at 390px; hand fixes recorded

onyx.note: One real export so far, the locker hotspot photo. It brought a new item type, two hand fixes to the export, and a PNG-to-JPEG recompression that halved the portal.

phases.title: Reports and data
phases.goal: The owner's Reports page reading the client's own exports: a converter per export, written against their real columns, with a worked example generated by the same arithmetic.
phases.owner: us; the client supplies one real month of each export
inputs: One real export per report, with identifiers tokenised before it reaches us

steps.title: Get one real month of the export; keep the source files out of the repository
Profile it in the workbench: fill, types, faults, vocabulary columns versus prose
Decide the definitions that move the headline (what counts as a conversion) with the client
Write the sample: real structured columns, synthetic free text carrying the same tags
Add the converter config: expect roles and match fragments, required roles, vocabulary, patterns; status ready
Generate the Insights worked example
List every other export as planned, so the owner sees what is read and what is still to build

gate.label: at least one converter marked ready

gate.text: The first imported month checked against a number the client already knows

onyx.note: GymMaster task report, 90 rows. Tours convert at 71.4% against 15.4% for walk-ins. Conversion counts the export's own flag; rates under eight rows are shown and marked low, never withheld.

phases.title: Hosting and install
phases.goal: The portal live on its own subdomain over HTTPS, installable on a phone, updating on every push.
phases.owner: us; the client's DNS owner if it is their domain
inputs: A subdomain and who controls its DNS

steps.title: Build the hosted folder
Create the Cloudflare Pages project: no build, output clients/{slug}/site
Test on the *.pages.dev URL, then add the custom domain and wait for the certificate
Zone settings: Browser Cache TTL respects headers, Rocket Loader off, Always Use HTTPS on
Run the six checks: padlock, manifest, worker, offline reload, no-cache on sw.js, install on Android and iPhone

gate.label: hosted build matches the current config

gate.text: Live on {slug}.<domain> with a certificate; all six checks in the playbook passed

onyx.effort: about twenty minutes for the next client

phases.title: QA and walkthrough
phases.goal: Proof, before anyone outside the team sees it, that every audience gets a working portal on a phone and on a desktop.
inputs: A build that passes Phases 2 and 3

steps.title: Run the smoke test: every audience, every page, no errors, nothing empty, nothing wider than a phone
Walk the script on a real phone: landing, name, a simulation to completion, a guide ticked through, a wrong key then the right one, an export from Me
File-alone test: copy the single file into an empty folder and open it
Run the pitfalls list in the QA playbook against anything new in the engine

gate.text: Walkthrough script done on a real phone and on a desktop

onyx.note: Every bug in the pitfalls list was caught in a render pass, not by a test. The smoke test exists so the next client does not depend on someone looking.

phases.title: Handover and sign-off
phases.goal: The client has the portal, the keys, the open items and the one caveat they must hear from us, and has confirmed or replaced every demo item.

steps.title: Send the link (or the single file) and, separately, the keys
Send the handover pack: what is live, what is demo, the open asks, how corrections reach us
Say the iOS caveat out loud: an installed app has its own storage, and progress is per device
Take the client's corrections, clear demo flags as content is confirmed, rebuild, bump the version

gate.text: Keys delivered separately from the link
iOS storage and per-device progress caveat raised with the client

onyx.note: ONYX is a showcase: 62 demo flags and five open asks stand, which is correct for where it is.

phases.title: Run and iterate
phases.goal: The portal stays true: processes reviewed on their cycle, corrections in within the week, every release versioned.
phases.owner: us, on a cadence agreed at handover
inputs: Corrections from the portal's 'Something wrong?' route
Exported process drafts and posts from the client's devices

steps.title: Take in exported drafts and posts: a draft with resolves replaces its gap, it does not sit beside it
Review processes that are past their cycle
Rebuild both targets and push; Pages deploys; bump the version and write the changelog line

gate.label: no process past its review cycle
